dossier.public_summary: The 10.8-day 450 ppm dip co-varies strongly between sectors and individual transits and shows a deep ~179 ppm secondary eclipse plus odd-even differences, best matching a blended eclipsing binary rather than a planet on the target.

reasons.why: Depth varies by factor ~10 between sectors and not as a calibration offset, inconsistent with a planet on the target.
reasons.value: p_constant=1.603e-8 depth_change_pct=232.8 per_sector 14:44 err178,15:908 err144,74:1114 err200,48:90 err157,75:214 err88

reasons.why: Two very deep outliers plus inconsistency and high contribution from top 3 drives the average, expected from a blended eclipsing binary not a stable planet.
reasons.value: share_of_top_3=0.816, chi2=135.92 dof14 p_consistent=4.5748599468650305e-22, outliers 1736 ppm sigma6.8 and 2025 ppm sigma5.9

reasons.why: Secondary dip seen at ~0.43 phase well above noise with depth ~41% of primary indicates a stellar companion eclipse, not a planet.
Odd/even depth difference significant, supporting eclipse at twice reported period or an active EB folded at half period.
Low planet-like score consistent with EB indicators above; RUWE=1.295 and plausible blended NEB (closest that could 45.4 arcsec eclipse_needed0.0051) further favour neighbour/blend.
